thread:
Isha Patel: Heads up — smoke tests for canary rollout are hitting OOMs in the KV cache after today's kernel-selection merge. Repro 2/5 on small harness, failing on staging GPUs.
Ryan Cho: Link to the failing run? logs?
Isha Patel: https://ci.internal/runs/8002 — core snippet below. Repro on n1-standard-8 with GPU.
Isha Patel: ```
2026-03-18T10:12:04Z runtime ERROR: allocate slab failed: OOM (req 12MB)
proc=serving-12 node=gs-rlu-06 pool=kv-slab-3 seqLen=2048 live=1.9GB free=120MB
2026-03-18T10:12:04Z runtime DEBUG: evict window scanned 512 entries, freed 1 entry
```
Oliver Nguyen: fwiw the kernel-router change biases fast-path kernels for seqLen>1024. That could increase per-entry metadata or change alignment -> fragmentation.
Marta Ruiz: I ran a micro-profiler for the same workload. heaplet churn +3x, allocs in 64-256B range skyrocketed. Small table from profiler: 
```
slot_class, allocs/sec
64B, 19800
128B, 11200
256B, 4300
```
Samir Khan: sounds like alloc pattern shifted. Can we confirm whether kernel_select now stores extra per-kv pointer or padding?
Isha Patel: grep of runtime changes shows addition of `struct kernel_meta { uint32_t id; uint16_t flags; uint16_t pad; }` in hot path. That pad might be aligning entries to 16B more often.
Ryan Cho: deploy-bot reported CI smoke fail for canary: `ci/canary-smoke #439 FAILED` (dev-bot pinned).
dev-bot: ci/canary-smoke reported 17% increase in mem high-water on staging canary.
Oliver Nguyen: hypothesis: kernel selection change increased per-entry footprint -> same cache capacity holds fewer entries -> eviction rate up -> more misses and more allocations -> fragmentation.
Marta Ruiz: I tried setting KV_EVICT_WINDOW=4 locally — OOMs reduced in 1/3 runs but throughput dropped ~30%. kv_hit_rate fell from 72% -> 40% when window shrank.
Samir Khan: we should bisect between commits `abc1234` (pre-merge) and `def5678` (post-merge). I can run binary-bisect on staging.
Ryan Cho: quick bisect script: `./tools/bisect_kv.sh --range abc1234..def5678 --harness ./tools/kv_smoke --seed 42`
Isha Patel: also enabling `KV_ALLOC_PROF=1` yields this sample: `entries_allocated: 1.2M, avg_entry_bytes=80 -> 104 after merge` — delta ~24 bytes/entry.
Oliver Nguyen: if average increases by ~24 bytes and we have ~50M entries in pool, that's ~1.2GB delta which matches the observed memory pressure spike.
Marta Ruiz: created a rollback draft: https://phabricator/internal/pull/430-revert-kernel-router — marking as rollout-hold candidate.
Samir Khan: please add a perf CI test that includes skewed seqlen distribution (lots of 1024-4096) so we catch this earlier.
Isha Patel: added to the rollout hold channel and pinged @oncall. For now please don't promote canary -> stable.
dev-bot: incident created: INC-2026-03-18-01 (kv-cache OOM surge on canary).
Ryan Cho: quick mitigate suggestion: set env `KV_SLOT_STRIDE=2` (coarser packing) or temporarily increase pool size on canary nodes. Either buys time.
Oliver Nguyen: I'll run the bisect against a staging image and post results by EOD. Running `./tools/run_kv_stress --seqs 128,512,2048 --concurrency 8 --iter 200` now.
Marta Ruiz: also enabling `kv_alloc_debug=true` gave clearer stack traces pointing to `kernel_select_fastpath()` as the hot allocator.
Samir Khan: ACK. If bisect pins it to the kernel-router change I'll submit the revert and we can iterate on alignment and reduce padding.
Isha Patel: TL;DR: regressions started after kernel-selection merge, memory delta ~24B/entry, causes fragmentation & OOMs on high-seqlen workloads. Rollout on hold; bisect + rollback PR in progress. :eyes: :exclamation:
Ryan Cho: +1 to hold and revert if bisect confirms. Thanks for quick triage. :thumbsup:
Oliver Nguyen: will update thread with bisect sha and perf traces.
Marta Ruiz: filing perf CI ticket: PERF-723 (add seqlen skew test).
Isha Patel: leaving logs and core dumps in `/tmp/kv-oom-8002/` on staging host for postmortem.
Ryan Cho: noted.
